Subject: Handoff cadence & acceptance gates for Redwood rollout

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our discussion, I attached a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the high-level milestones, proposed owners, and acceptance gates we think make sense for the initial Redwood deployment at Sierra Logistics. Key points in the spreadsheet:

- Phase 1 (Sandbox & Integration): connect APIs, ingest minimal dataset for mapping (owner: Sierra Eng). Acceptance gate: API keys exchange completed + 2 smoke tests passing. Target: Dec 21.
- Phase 2 (Pilot/P0): limited production traffic to 5% of requests; Redwood dedicated pool configured. Acceptance gate: latency <200ms P95 and no regression on 3 core prompts. Target: Jan 15.
- Phase 3 (Go-Live): phased cutover and runbook handoff to ops. Acceptance gate: UAT sign-off + documented rollback plan. Target: Feb 2.

Can you review the milestones and the acceptance-gate language and flag any items that need adjusting? Two specific asks:
1) Confirm the UAT exit criteria Sierra requires (we put a draft in the MAP: functional coverage + sample QA run).
2) Confirm the primary integration owner and backup (we listed Miguel Santos as primary in the sheet).

Attachments: Sierra_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.xlsx, Redwood_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (SOW shows proposed timeline and payment milestones).

If it looks good, I'll schedule a short alignment call next week to finalize owners and sign SOW.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0198

Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan and the file. I reviewed the MAP and the SOW PDF and added a few comments to the SOW (attached as Sierra_SOW_comments_20261205.pdf). Two quick notes from Sierra:

- UAT exit criteria: We require 95% task-success on the acceptance test suite (we sent an example test set in a separate note) AND completion of a 48-hour stability window with no critical errors. Can you confirm Redwood can commit to the 48-hour stability window as an automated check prior to sign-off?
- Integration owner: Miguel is currently the primary contact but will be unavailable Dec 28–Jan 4. Can we list Jaime Flores as the interim contact for that week and keep Miguel as lead?

Procurement looped in for SOW redlines — they asked if we can target signature by Dec 22 to allow provisioning in January.

I can do a quick joint call on Monday afternoon (Dec 8) to run through the acceptance gates if that helps.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz

Adding a few operational clarifications from the CS/Implementation side before we confirm:

Ben — good summary. Two proposed edits to the acceptance gates to reduce ambiguity:

- "48-hour stability window" -> define as "48 consecutive hours with no P1/P2 errors and P95 latency within agreed threshold for production-like traffic." Owner: Redwood SRE (Marissa).
- "UAT sign-off" -> split into: functional sign-off (Sierra PM) and performance sign-off (Redwood SRE). Both signatures required; we will provide a short checklist for each.

Suggested owners and immediate commitments:
- Redwood kickoff & runbook creation: Marissa (CS) + Tessa (implementation lead). Deliverable: runbook draft by Dec 18.
- Integration health checks and automated stability: Karthik (Platform Eng). He will scope the monitoring dashboard and 48-hour automation by Dec 17.
- SOW and billing: Ben to coordinate with Procurement; Marissa will prepare acceptance checklist to be attached to the SOW.

I recommend we accept the interim contact for Miguel (Jaime) and publish an updated contact list in the MAP. We should lock the SOW sign date target Dec 22 but make the provisioning window contingent on payment terms — call that out explicitly.

If Ben can confirm the Monday Dec 8 call with Lena, I will prepare the runbook template and pre-populate the acceptance checklist so we can iterate live on the call.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
